name: Closing Disclosure
what: CFPB-mandated disclosure summarizing final loan terms, projected payments, and closing costs.
why: Allows the borrower to review the transaction’s final disclosed financial terms.
interaction: Signer reviews and signs or acknowledges receipt where the package directs.
focus: Locate signatures/dates and follow presentation instructions without interpreting figures.
notarized: Usually no; verify the actual form.
guidance: Identify the title and direct the signer to the disclosed sections without characterizing the deal.
do_not: Do not explain whether APR, cash to close, fees, or terms are correct or favorable.
questions: Refer financial, lender, settlement, and discrepancy questions to the named lender/title contact.
source: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau — Closing Disclosure and closing-document guidance.

name: Promissory Note
packages: Buyer/Purchase; Refinance; HELOC or product-specific note; Reverse Mortgage note(s)
what: The borrower’s written promise to repay under stated terms.
why: Evidence of the debt and repayment obligation.
interaction: Borrower signs exactly as directed; initials may appear where specified.
focus: Names, signature capacity, required dates, and package-version integrity.
guidance: State that it is the note and point to the lender-provided payment/term sections if instructed.
do_not: Do not interpret interest, default, prepayment, or enforceability.
questions: Refer term/payment/legal questions to lender or ordering party.
source: CFPB closing guidance; Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac Uniform Notes; HUD HECM model notes.

name: Deed of Trust / Mortgage / Security Instrument
packages: Buyer/Purchase; Refinance; HELOC; Reverse Mortgage security instruments
what: Instrument securing the debt with an interest in the described property.
why: Creates the collateral/security relationship and is generally recorded.
interaction: Required property owners/borrowers sign in stated capacities.
focus: Correct version, property/address context, names/capacities, riders, signatures, certificate.
notarized: Commonly, but not automatically; inspect the actual certificate and instructions.
guidance: Identify the document and signature/certificate locations only.
do_not: Do not explain foreclosure, lien priority, homestead effect, or legal consequences.
source: CFPB closing guidance; Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac Uniform Security Instruments; HUD model mortgages.

name: Notice of Right to Cancel
packages: Certain refinance/home-secured credit transactions; not ordinary purchase closings
what: Notice of a statutory rescission period when applicable.
why: Provides required cancellation timing and method for covered transactions.
interaction: Signer acknowledges receipt and dates/copies as directed.
focus: Correct transaction/date/copy count and ordering-party instructions.
guidance: Point to the printed deadline/method without calculating or advising.
do_not: Do not tell a signer whether a transaction is rescindable or calculate a disputed deadline.
questions: Refer coverage/deadline questions to lender/title or legal counsel.
source: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau — right of rescission guidance.

name: Initial Escrow Account Disclosure
what: Estimate of escrow deposits and projected disbursements.
why: Explains how taxes/insurance may be collected and paid from escrow.
interaction: Signer reviews and signs/acknowledges if directed.
focus: Signature/acknowledgment placement and package completeness.
guidance: Identify the escrow disclosure and let the signer review figures.
do_not: Do not predict shortages, tax changes, or future payments.
source: CFPB mortgage-closing guidance and actual lender disclosure.

name: First Payment Letter / Payment Coupon
what: Operational payment instructions showing initial due date, amount, and destination.
why: Helps the borrower make the first scheduled payment.
interaction: Signer reviews and retains the appropriate copy.
focus: Do not separate borrower-retained pages from the package incorrectly.
notarized: No, absent an unusual actual certificate.
guidance: Point to the printed instructions.
do_not: Do not change payment instructions or accept payment unless expressly authorized.
source: Actual lender/servicer document and assignment instructions.

name: Occupancy Affidavit
what: Statement concerning intended or actual occupancy.
why: Supports underwriting and loan-program representations.
interaction: Signer reads, completes only permitted factual blanks, and signs as directed.
focus: Names, property, permitted completion, signature, and actual certificate.
notarized: Often contains a certificate; verify actual document.
guidance: Invite the signer to read the statement and answer only for themselves.
do_not: Do not advise which occupancy status to select.
source: Actual package; Fannie Mae special-purpose forms where applicable.

name: Signature / Name Affidavit
packages: Purchase; Refinance; Seller; HELOC; other packages
what: Statement connecting name variations or signatures to the signer.
why: Supports identity/name consistency across transaction records.
interaction: Signer reviews listed variations, reports inaccuracies, and signs as directed.
focus: Never force acceptance of an incorrect name; inspect actual certificate.
guidance: Ask the signer to review each variation and refer corrections.
do_not: Do not invent aliases or tell the signer to claim a name they dispute.
questions: Pause and contact ordering party for inaccurate/missing variations.
source: Actual title/lender package and authorized instructions.

name: Compliance Agreement / Errors & Omissions Agreement
packages: Purchase; Refinance; HELOC; some seller packages
what: Agreement to cooperate with permitted post-closing corrections or omitted administrative items.
why: Supports correction of defined clerical/compliance issues.
interaction: Signer reads and signs as directed.
focus: Document title, signature and actual certificate; distinguish from E&O insurance.
notarized: May be; verify the actual certificate.
guidance: Identify the document without describing the scope beyond its text.
do_not: Do not promise what corrections may be demanded or interpret legal limits.
source: Actual lender/title document; package instructions.

name: IRS / Tax Forms (for example W-9, 4506-C where present)
what: Taxpayer identification or transcript authorization forms included for the transaction.
why: Supports lender verification/reporting requirements.
interaction: Signer verifies taxpayer information and signs as directed.
focus: Correct form/version, signature/date, no copying sensitive data into APS notes.
guidance: Identify the form and signature area only.
do_not: Do not provide tax advice or complete taxpayer elections.
questions: Refer tax/content questions to lender or tax professional.
source: Actual IRS/lender form and package instructions.

name: Insurance Documents
packages: Purchase; Refinance; Reverse Mortgage; some HELOC
what: Evidence, authorization, or acknowledgment concerning required property insurance.
why: Supports collateral protection and closing conditions.
interaction: Signer reviews and signs/acknowledges where directed.
focus: Keep policy/data pages in order and protect personal information.
notarized: Usually no unless actual certificate says otherwise.
guidance: Identify as insurance-related package material.
do_not: Do not advise coverage sufficiency or policy selection.
source: Actual insurer/lender/title documents.

name: Title and Settlement Documents
what: Title, settlement, closing, disbursement, and ownership-related documents prepared for the transaction.
why: Coordinate conveyance, settlement, payoff, fees, and title requirements.
interaction: Parties review and sign the forms assigned to them.
focus: Ordering-party instructions, capacity, signature lines, notarization certificate, copy/return requirements.
guidance: Present by exact title and keep the package order.
do_not: Do not interpret title condition, ownership, prorations, or legal effect.
source: Actual title/settlement package; CFPB closing guidance where applicable.

name: Deed
what: Instrument conveying an interest in real property.
why: Transfers the described property interest when validly executed/delivered/recorded.
interaction: Authorized grantor(s) sign in stated capacity.
focus: Exact names/capacities, property reference, signature, witnesses if required, actual certificate.
guidance: Identify the deed and signature/certificate areas.
do_not: Do not choose deed type, advise ownership effect, or alter legal description.
source: Actual deed and jurisdiction/ordering-party authority.

name: Seller Affidavits
what: Seller statements about ownership, liens, occupancy, repairs, identity, or transaction facts.
why: Supports title/settlement review and risk allocation.
interaction: Seller reads, supplies only their facts, and signs as directed.
focus: No coaching; verify actual certificate and completeness.
notarized: Frequently but variably; inspect actual form.
guidance: Ask the seller to review the statement and refer uncertainty.
do_not: Do not answer factual/legal questions for the seller.
source: Actual title/settlement package.

name: Payoff Authorization
what: Authorization to obtain, confirm, or transmit payoff information.
why: Supports satisfaction of existing obligations at closing.
interaction: Authorized party reviews account/property information and signs.
focus: Correct account/party, privacy, signature, and transmission path.
guidance: Identify the authorization and protect account information.
do_not: Do not calculate payoff or promise disbursement timing.
source: Actual title/lender/servicer form.

name: HELOC Agreement / Note
what: Product-specific agreement or note governing a revolving home-equity line.
why: States borrowing, repayment, advance, rate, and account terms.
interaction: Borrower signs/initials as directed.
focus: Correct product/version, signatures, and package instructions.
guidance: Identify it as the HELOC agreement/note.
do_not: Do not explain draws, rates, tax effects, or suitability.
source: Actual lender document; Fannie Mae special-purpose guidance where applicable.

name: HELOC Security Instrument
what: Instrument securing the HELOC with the property.
why: Creates the product’s collateral relationship and may be recorded.
interaction: Required owners/borrowers sign in stated capacities.
focus: Names, property, riders, signatures, and actual certificate.
guidance: Identify title/signature/certificate locations.
do_not: Do not explain lien priority or Texas home-equity law.
source: Actual lender/title instrument and applicable authoritative instructions.

name: Loan Modification Agreement
what: Agreement changing specified terms of an existing loan.
why: Documents the servicer/lender-approved modification.
interaction: Borrower reviews and signs as directed.
focus: Correct borrower/loan/version, signature/date, and actual certificate.
guidance: Identify the agreement and let the signer read the stated changes.
do_not: Do not explain eligibility, affordability, or legal consequences.
questions: Refer to servicer/lender/housing counselor or attorney.
source: Actual servicer/lender agreement; HUD model modification documents where applicable.

name: Reverse Mortgage Note(s)
what: HECM or proprietary reverse-mortgage debt instrument(s); HUD HECM packages may contain multiple notes.
why: Evidence obligations under the reverse-mortgage structure.
interaction: Borrower(s) sign as directed; package may distinguish first/second instruments.
focus: Do not omit paired documents; verify names, capacities, versions, signatures.
guidance: Identify each note by its exact title and sequence.
do_not: Do not explain loan economics, benefits, or estate consequences.
source: HUD HECM model documents; actual proprietary package.

name: Reverse Mortgage Security Instrument(s)
what: HECM/proprietary mortgage or deed-of-trust instruments; HUD HECM may include first and second instruments.
why: Secures obligations under the reverse-mortgage structure.
interaction: Required borrowers/owners sign in stated capacities.
focus: Paired instruments, riders, property, signatures, certificates, package order.
guidance: Present each instrument by exact title.
do_not: Do not interpret lien structure, foreclosure, occupancy, or succession rights.
source: HUD HECM model mortgages; actual package.

name: Reverse Mortgage Disclosures / Loan Agreement
what: Program/product disclosures and agreement describing advances, charges, payment plan, and borrower responsibilities.
why: Documents program terms and required acknowledgments.
interaction: Borrower reviews and signs/acknowledges as directed.
focus: Correct versions, all required signatures, retain copies, no interpretation.
guidance: Identify exact document names and allow appropriate review time.
do_not: Do not recommend payment options or explain financial suitability.
source: HUD HECM model documents and actual lender package.

name: Non-Borrowing Spouse Documents
what: Certifications, acknowledgments, or property-right documents for an eligible or other non-borrowing spouse.
why: Addresses program and property-right requirements defined by the actual transaction.
interaction: Named spouse reviews and signs only documents assigned to that capacity.
focus: Identity/capacity, correct document set, signatures, actual certificates.
guidance: Use the package’s exact capacity language.
do_not: Do not determine eligibility, property rights, or future occupancy protections.
source: HUD Borrower and Non-Borrowing Spouse Certifications; actual package.
